script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Family
Theme: second chances

Begin screenplay.

TITLE: The Lost Son

INT. KITCHEN - MORNING

A cozy kitchen in the suburbs. JASON, a 40s man with a kind face, is making breakfast for his WIFE, RACHEL, who sits at the table, sipping her coffee.

JASON
(cheerfully)
Good morning, love. How did you sleep?

RACHEL
(smiling)
Great. How about you?

JASON
(sighs)
I've been better.

INT. LIVING ROOM - DAY

Jason sits on the couch, staring at the family photo on the mantel. His oldest son, MIKE, a rebellious teenager, is in the photo, but he's missing from the present. Rachel enters and sits beside Jason.

RACHEL
(concerned)
What's been on your mind?

JASON
(sighs)
Mike.

RACHEL
(nods)
I know. But he's just going through a phase.

JASON
(desperately)
I can't let him destroy his life, Rachel.

INT. SCHOOL - DAY

Jason walks into the principal's office. Principal JAMES greets him warmly.

PRINCIPAL JAMES
(smiling)
Good to see you again, Jason. What brings you here today?

JASON
(sternly)
I need to talk about my son, Mike.

PRINCIPAL JAMES
(nods)
Yes, he's had some challenges this year. But he's shown improvement.

JASON
(insistent)
I want to help him. I want to give him a second chance.

INT. GYM - DAY

Jason meets with COACH THOMAS, who runs a local boxing gym. They talk about Mike's problems and how boxing could help him.

COACH THOMAS
(firmly)
I can give him a chance, Jason. But he has to want it.

INT. LIVING ROOM - EVENING

Rachel is watching a documentary about boxing when Mike enters. She turns to him with a concerned look.

RACHEL
(worried)
You look tired, Mike. Are you okay?

MIKE
(sarcastically)
I'm great. Just had a long day at school.

RACHEL
(persistent)
You know your dad is worried about you.

MIKE
(frustrated)
He just doesn't understand.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

Jason and Mike sit across from each other at a table. They exchange awkward small talk.

MIKE
(angrily)
You think you know what's best for me?

JASON
(calmly)
I want what's best for you, Mike.

MIKE
(bitterly)
You abandoned me when I needed you the most.

JASON
(sighs)
I made a mistake, Mike. I'm sorry.

MIKE
(sternly)
Sorry doesn't cut it.

INT. BOXING GYM - DAY

Mike begins training at the gym. Jason watches from the sidelines, proud of his son's determination.

INT. LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

Rachel and Jason sit together, watching as Mike practices boxing moves in the living room.

RACHEL
(smiling)
He's really trying, isn't he?

JASON
(smiling back)
Yes, he is.

INT. BOXING GYM - NIGHT

Mike competes in his first boxing match. Jason and Rachel cheer him on from the sidelines. Mike wins, and they all share a proud moment.

INT. LIVING ROOM - EVENING

Jason, Rachel, and Mike sit together, enjoying a family dinner.

RACHEL
(looking around the table)
This is where we belong.

MIKE
(gratefully)
Thanks, Dad.

JASON
(smiling)
We're a team, Mike. Always have been, always will be.

Fade out.

End screenplay.
